reference_sources.via: reference-libraries — structural authority behind the `owl` template. Section order and component set only; none of Owl's brand program names are used.
reference_sources.reason_not_scraped: The owl template in astro-templates/owl already encodes this reference. Re-scraping would cost money and add nothing.

vertical_library_note: No office-technology/B2B-IT library exists. `default` supplies the anti-patterns; the owl template supplies structure. Roofing/concrete libraries were deliberately NOT used — their photography and copy direction are home-services specific.

palette_rationale.accent: The client's own brand red, extracted from their live CSS (#DF0028). Kept exactly — it is the single most recognizable thing about the GBM brand.
palette_rationale.primary: Deep slate. GBM's existing site already uses a slate CTA band; a near-neutral dark lets the red stay the only saturated color on the page and reads correctly for a B2B audience.
palette_rationale.accent_ink: Darkened brand red for accent-colored TEXT on light backgrounds. #DF0028 measures 5.04:1 on white and 4.66:1 on the light surface — both pass AA — but #C8001F gives 6.04:1 of headroom across every light tone the template uses.
palette_rationale.accent_on_dark: The template uses --color-accent as TEXT on --color-primary bands (Testimonials eyebrow/stars, ProcessSteps label, WhyChooseUs counters). #DF0028 measures only 2.89:1 there and fails AA. #FF7383 measures 5.79:1 on #1C2733 while still reading unmistakably as the GBM red. This is the inverse of the template default's problem (its gold fails on LIGHT, GBM's red fails on DARK), so a new token is required and the dark-band components are patched to use it.
palette_rationale.on_accent: White on #DF0028 is 5.04:1 — passes AA for button labels at any size.

typography.source: Both detected on the client's live site (Poppins headings, Open Sans body). Kept rather than overridden with the template default (Montserrat/Inter) so the rebuild still reads as GBM.

spacing.note: Template defaults retained unchanged. No spacing values were taken from the client's site.

motion.note: Template defaults only. No motion or animation was extracted from the client's site.

imagery_direction: Real Canon hardware in real offices — GBM's own product photography where available.
Northeastern PA office/commercial interiors, not generic 'diverse team in a glass boardroom' stock.
Partner logos (Canon, HP, Microsoft, uniFLOW, PaperCut, Cisco, EFI, N-able) as monochrome trust marks, not decorative color blocks.
No handshake photos, no cartoon flat-illustration icon sets — the existing site's six red line-art industry icons are exactly what to avoid repeating.
anti_patterns: randomized section order — use the fixed owl order
'Trusted by 10,000+ businesses' claims with no source — GBP shows 4 reviews at 4.0
red line-art icon grids that compete with the red CTA for attention (carried over from the client's current site)
home-services framing: financing offers, seasonal/weather hooks, 'protect your home' language
leading with a product SKU instead of a customer outcome (the current site's hero mistake)
template_deviations: Financing section disabled — irrelevant to a B2B office-equipment purchase committee (GBM's leasing is handled through Canon Financial, not a consumer finance widget).
us_vs_them section disabled — naming competitors is in the avoid list from local research.
Trust-badge rating chip suppressed on the hero: 4 Google reviews is too thin to display as social proof.
Dark-band accent text switched from --color-accent to --color-accent-on-dark for AA compliance.
